title: Congestion-aware circuit breaker and quarantine lanes for Dedicated capacity
creator: Maya Chen
description: PRD for a congestion-aware circuit breaker + quarantine lane mechanism for Dedicated capacity. Goal: limit tenant-induced noisy-neighbor effects during transient hotspots while preserving predictable SLOs for committed tenants and enabling safe burst/fallback behavior. This is an ops-safe control that integrates with reserved pools, autoscaler signals, and fallback model routing.
goals: Protect committed-reservation SLOs (p50/p95/p99 token latency and throughput guarantees) during tenant hotspots
Provide an automatic, observable quarantine path to temporarily limit a tenant's resource footprint without immediate eviction
Integrate with reserved-pool autoscale events to gracefully degrade tenants into cheaper/isolated variants (e.g., lower-q model or throttled concurrency)
Emit clear telemetry and operator alerts for quarantine actions and circuit-breaker triggers
success_metrics: Reduction in p99 latency tail spikes for non-offending tenants in the same pool by >= 80% during injected hotspot tests
Quarantine actions reduce global 95th percentile GPU utilization variance across tenants by >= 60% in chaos runs
Automated quarantine triggers correctly avoid hard evictions in 95% of simulated overload scenarios
Console surfaces quarantine state and reason within 30s of trigger in 95% of cases
scope_in_scope: Circuit-breaker rules (thresholds, cool-downs) evaluated in serving runtime using telemetry (queue length, per-tenant token rate, GPU util, p95 latency)
Tenant quarantine lane: reduced concurrency / enforced rate limit + routing to fallback model variant or billing throttle
Operator controls: manual quarantine, undo, severity override, and list of quarantined tenants in Console
Telemetry: telemetry events, audit log entries, and dashboard panels for quarantine/circuit-breaker activity
Integration with Dedicated autoscaler to preferentially prewarm or backoff during quarantine transitions
scope_out_of_scope: Changes to host-level networking or hypervisor scheduling
Billing model changes beyond telemetry tagging (we will mark events for downstream billing teams but not change invoices in initial scope)
Cross-region failover or multi-zone rebalancing (future work)
requirements: R1: Runtime must evaluate per-tenant moving-window metrics (1m, 5m) and compute a congestion score
R2: Circuit-breaker must expose configurable thresholds: token-rate, pending-requests, p95 latency delta, gpu_util_pct
R3: When triggered, quarantine lane reduces tenant concurrency by configurable percent and can route to a designated fallback model OR apply a soft-throttle
R4: Quarantine duration should be configurable with exponential backoff (default 2m -> 8m -> 32m) and manual reset
R5: All actions must be recorded to audit logs with reason, metric snapshot, and operator who acted (if manual)
R6: Console must show active quarantines, past events, and provide one-click manual override; API for programmatic overrides
R7: Metrics must be emitted to telemetry pipeline with a consistent schema (tenant_id, pool_id, trigger_type, metric_snapshot, severity, action_taken)
R8: Rollout to prod must be gated by an incremental feature flag per-pool and include a synthetic traffic canary and a 10% customer shadow test
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): implement runtime evaluation + telemetry events; run targeted fault injection tests on staging clusters
Phase 2 (canary): enable circuit-breaker for 5 internal customers in a non-critical pool; monitor KPIs for 72h
Phase 3 (gradual): enable on 10% of pools with shadow actions for 7 days, then soft-enforce for 24h
Phase 4 (global): enable for all Dedicated pools with operator runbook and postmortem playbook available
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Circuit-breaker triggers when enforced thresholds are breached and emits telemetry event within 10s
AC-2: Quarantined tenant sees enforced concurrency reduction and/or routing to fallback variant; downstream model requests succeed with 200 or 429 depending on configured action
AC-3: Non-offending tenants' p99 latency during an injected hotspot remains within 1.1x of baseline in 90% of runs
AC-4: Audit log contains at least: timestamp, tenant_id, pool_id, trigger_metric_values, action_taken, duration, operator (if manual)
AC-5: Console UI displays quarantine state and link to an incident timeline; operator override API documented and tested
AC-6: Playbook and runbook validated with oncall through tabletop and one live drill without customer-visible downtime
AC-7: Rollout feature flag can be toggled per-pool without requiring service restart
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: False positives cause unnecessary throttles -> Mitigation: conservative default thresholds, shadow mode, and short initial quarantine windows
Risk: Quarantine complexity increases oncall cognitive load -> Mitigation: clear UI, concise alerts, and automated suggested remediation in Console
Risk: Integration gaps with autoscaler may cause oscillation -> Mitigation: add hysteresis and require autoscaler acknowledgement of state change before scaling down aggressive backfills
Risk: Customers perceive covert throttling -> Mitigation: provide tenant-facing reason codes and optional customer notifications via webhook
dependencies: ENG-2711 (fallback routing API and model-variant tagging)
PM-520481 (reserved-capacity surface redesign for Console integration)
